Plot Associations Between Two Tables

Source: R/cross_assoc.r
plot.ecodive_cross_assoc.Rd

The heatmap of a cross_assoc() result: one row per feature of x, one column per variable of y, coloured by the correlation, with stars on the cells whose adjusted p-values are small.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_cross_assoc'
plot(
  x,
  n_x = 30,
  n_y = 30,
  clust = "average",
  stars = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  col = NULL,
  key = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A cross_assoc() result.

n_x, n_y

The most features of x (rows) and variables of y (columns) to show: those with the smallest adjusted p-value (ties broken by the largest \(|r|\)). Default: 30 each.

clust

'average' (the default) orders the rows and the columns by average-linkage clustering (stats::hclust()) on \(1 - r\) between their profiles of correlations in the shown block; any other method of stats::hclust() also works. 'none' keeps the input order.

stars

Thresholds of the adjusted p-values for *, **, *** (any number of them, largest first). Default: c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001). NULL marks the cells with reject by a dot instead.

col

Colours for the scale from -1 to 1. Default: the diverging hcl.colors(65, "Blue-Red 3").

key

Whether to draw the colour key. Default: TRUE.

...

Passed on to graphics::image(), such as main, xlab and ylab.

Value

x, invisibly.

Examples

    set.seed(1)
    counts <- matrix(rpois(30 * 8, 20), 30, 8,
      dimnames = list(NULL, paste0('Taxon', 1:8)))
    env <- data.frame(pH = counts[, 1] / 10 + rnorm(30), temp = rnorm(30))
    plot(cross_assoc(counts, env))
